newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: No guarantees from China on Australian wool - IWS.
newsitem.headline: No guarantees from China on Australian wool - IWS.

text.p: Any undertaking given in Australia by Chinese vice-premier Zhu Rongji that China would increase its purchases of Australia wool had not been backed by specific guarantees, Alec Morrison, chairman of the International Wool Secretariat, told Reuters.

However Morrison, speaking at the Wool Council of Australia (WCA) annual conference, said that despite the lack of guarantees, prospects appeared better for China to increase its purchase of Australian wool.
Asked how the Chinese government might be responsible for increased purchases of Australian wool, Morrison said there were still major state-owned wool-using operations in China.

He also said China had a population of 100 million on its eastern seaboard with annual income of more than A$1,000 per head. This was projected to increase to 200 million above that income figure by year 2000. Projections such as this indicated increased demand for wool, he said.

In an address to the conference, WCA president Rod Thirkell-Johnston said early success had been achieved in a "major push" for tariff reduction and better access for Australian wool to Mexico and India. A renewed effort was being undertaken with China and the United States, he said.
